formal_statement: ∃ L : Submodule ℂ (Fin 4 × Fin 5 → ℂ), (∀ t ∈ L, (∑ i : Fin 4, ∑ j, t (i, j)) = 0 ∧ (∑ j, ∑ l, if j = l then 0 else ∑ a : Fin 4, ∑ b : Fin 4, if a < b then t (a, j) * t (b, l) else 0) = 0 ∧ (∑ j, ∑ l, ∑ m, if j = l ∨ j = m ∨ l = m then 0 else ∑ a : Fin 4, ∑ b : Fin 4, ∑ c : Fin 4, if a < b ∧ b < c then t (a, j) * t (b, l) * t (c, m) else 0) = 0 ∧ (∑ j, ∑ l, ∑ m, ∑ n, if j = l ∨ j = m ∨ j = n ∨ l = m ∨ l = n ∨ m = n then 0 else t (0, j) * t (1, l) * t (2, m) * t (3, n)) = 0) ∧ 8 ≤ Module.finrank ℂ L
plain_statement: There is a linear space L of 4 x 5 complex matrices of dimension at least 8 such that, for every t in L, the entry sum and the sums of all 2 x 2, all 3 x 3 and all 4 x 4 subpermanents of t all vanish; that is, perm-type level at four rows. The conjectured bound is dim L <= p + q - 2 = 7; the best space known has dimension p + q - 3 = 6. A witness would refute the sharp form of the level-space bound at four rows. It may well not exist: this is a search, and a proof that no witness exists is not what this row asks.
title: SEARCH: a level space of 4 x 5 matrices of dimension at least 8 (would refute the bound p + q - 2 at four rows)
